video.title: EU4 1.36 The Papal State Guide - The Most UNDERRATED Nation For BLOBBING

items.label: Stay Curia controller
items.text: -10% stability cost, +1 diplomat, +20% advisor discount, -20% aggressive expansion. Keep it until the end.

items.label: Excommunicate before every war
items.text: Halves AE on provinces you border, and gives the Excommunicated Ruler CB. Check Papal Actions before declaring, and now and then for anyone you might fight later.

items.label: Indulgence blocks it
items.text: Nations that bought Indulgence for their sins, or that you like too much, can't be excommunicated.

items.label: Appoint Cardinal
items.text: +50 opinion with the target. Use it to reach 190 for diplo-vassalizing.

phases.name: Day one setup
phases.intro: Everything here happens before you unpause. Order inside a group doesn't matter unless it's numbered.

steps.text: Summon the Diet
steps.note: Pick whichever agenda suits you. You start with 50% crownland

steps.text: Clergy: Religious State, Clerical Advisory Council, Religious Diplomats, Clerical Education
Nobility: Primacy of the Nobility, Increased Levies, Aristocratic Counselors, Strong Duchies, Integration Policy
steps.note: Done in advance so subjects annex cheaply later

steps.text: Burghers: Land of Commerce, Patronage of the Arts, Commercial Advisory Board, Indebted to the Burghers
Seize land, never sell titles
steps.note: Money isn't a problem as the Pope

steps.text: Admin: inflation reduction
Diplo: improve relations or diplo rep
Mil: discipline, morale, fort defense or manpower
steps.note: He took discipline
Keep the third slot empty for Naples

steps.text: Ally
steps.note: Your first ally. Helps against HRE minors, or lets you join the HRE
A northern neighbour you won't fight soon
Castile if France won't. France is slightly better

steps.text: Scornfully insult
steps.note: Sets up excommunicating them later

steps.text: Spy network
steps.note: With your last diplomat, for claims on Naples

steps.text: Golden Bull: the -5% stability cost one
steps.note: Available once a day passes. Or wait for the Renaissance bull if you want to help other Catholics

steps.text: Lower army maintenance, turn off forts
Set subjects to Siege
Light ships: Protect Trade in Genoa, go home during war
Queue about 5 light ships and 10 galleys

chain: Move the Alexandria and Valencia merchants to Genoa and Venice
steps.note: Lowers aggressive expansion

phases.name: First years and missions
phases.intro: Waiting on Aragon to free Naples and France to drop Provence. Use the time on missions.

loadout.note: You can't afford a full one yet.
have: Austria and Milan allied, France on the way
Level 1 admin, diplo and mil advisors
Merchants establishing communities in Genoa and Venice

steps.text: Spare diplomats: improve relations with subjects and allies

chain: Accept their call into the England war
steps.note: You won't actually do anything in that war

steps.text: Catholic Conformity
steps.note: Once you have 3 allies. +100 diplo
They convert their Orthodox provinces, you get devotion
+10% merc discipline for 20 years, and the Papal Swiss Guard mercs cost no professionalism
Whether or not the Renaissance spawned on you. It's an age objective and speeds up the spread

phases.name: War with Naples
phases.intro: Naples is free and borders you, with few or no allies. This war should be very easy.

loadout.note: Avoid fighting anyone ahead of you in tech.
have: Swiss Guard mission done (+10% merc discipline for 20 years)

steps.text: Aragon's ruler dies and Naples is released
steps.note: Usually by 1450. He's only seen it not happen once

steps.text: Aragon event: option 2 (subjugation CB)
steps.note: Don't use that CB. Subjugation forces vassalization and costs too much AE

chain: Wait for them to rival back
Take the mission for a 62-tradition general
steps.note: No claim on Naples yet? Spy on them first. The general mission unlocks once you hire mercs, so don't recruit one

steps.text: Start a spy network on Provence
steps.note: They're your next war

steps.text: Declare: Excommunicated Ruler CB, else Conquest. Call Milan
steps.note: Never the subjugation CB

steps.text: Peace at about 40 AE
steps.note: Excom CB: the bigger chunk plus money and war reparations. Conquest CB: 3 provinces, no money, so the truce ends sooner

phases.name: War with Provence
phases.intro: France always drops Provence after their war with England, which leaves Provence with weak allies.

have: Tier 2 reform (Commercial Mission for a money run, Mission of Protection for crusades, External Mission for conquering Europe. He took Commercial)

steps.text: France has broken its alliance with Provence
steps.note: Check right after the Naples peace

chain: If you took Commercial: new merchant in Valencia, transfer to Genoa

steps.text: Diplomats: improve relations with the countries you angered
Excommunicate Naples as soon as Papal Actions allows
steps.note: Halves AE for your next war with them. He got it in Nov 1452

steps.text: Declare (Excom CB or Conquest), call Milan and Austria
Peace: 3 southern provinces, humiliate if still rivals, money

phases.name: Consolidate
phases.intro: Take a 2 to 3 year breather. Your two openers are done.

steps.text: Annex Perugia and Urbino
steps.note: Both at once. The first provinces you took are expensive to core

steps.text: Vatican Library mission
steps.note: Admin tech or army tradition option is slightly better than diplo. He took army tradition

chain: Pay off the first burgher loans
Marketplaces in centers of trade and estuaries (Rome, Urbino, Naples, Aix)

steps.text: Seize land whenever estates are above 50 loyalty
steps.note: Keep crownland above 30%

steps.text: Admin tech 5: Quality ideas
steps.note: Divine is fine but weaker for now

steps.text: Naval doctrine: galley combat ability
Italian minors in the HRE: join the HRE if you're done early (around 1452), or wait for them to leave
steps.note: They leave around 1462. Joining lets you fight them without fighting Austria

phases.name: Northern Italy and Naples again
phases.intro: No strict order from here. Fight whoever is easiest, always with the excommunication CB if you can.

have: Marketplaces in your centers of trade

steps.text: The Italian minors leave the HRE

chain: Wait for the truce to end
steps.note: Only if they're still independent. You'll feed them their Sicily cores later. Never conquer Sicily yourself

steps.text: Spy networks and claims on Siena, Florence, Savoy, Genoa
steps.note: Lower autonomy from time to time

steps.text: Government ability: Justified Wars
Tier 3 reform: Education of the Court
steps.note: Its advisor discount stacks with the curia's

chain: Find 1 or 2 province minors that would accept (Bologna, Corsica, Lucca, Saluzzo)
Ally, guarantee, gift, mil access, influence, subsidies
steps.note: The offer-vassalization list shows who would accept

chain: Wait for the Ottomans to attack Venice (or bring Austria)
Excommunicate Venice if you border them

steps.text: Peace: Istria, Zara, Spalato, Padua, Verona
steps.note: About 30 AE, no money so the truce ends faster

steps.text: Release Dalmatia as your subject
steps.note: Strong trade, army and navy ideas

steps.text: Build Your Own Navy mission once you have the boats
Admin tech 6: workshops in high-value goods provinces
More than 2 subjects: Strong Duchies and Integration Policy
Break the alliance with Milan once you border them

phases.name: War with Aragon
phases.intro: Optional, and only when Aragon is fighting someone else. In his game Castile and France were beating them.

loadout.note: Artillery joins the template. Arty gives siege bonuses against level 2 and 3 forts at 1, 4, 6, 8 and 10 regiments, so build as many as you can afford.
have: Dalmatia released, Naples vassalized if they were independent

steps.text: Aragon is weak or at war with bigger powers
Declare on Aragon
steps.note: He used reconquest of Messina

chain: Sicily cores to Naples, or one province to release Sicily

steps.text: Use favors with France to return your subjects' cores
steps.note: Gerona in Nov 1479, Roussillon in Mar 1481

phases.name: Economy and midgame
phases.intro: Expand and build at the same time. Benchmark: about 27 ducats a month in 1480 with armies and forts up.

have: Admin tech 7: Trade ideas (Religious if you're going crusading)
Tier 4 reform (Head of the Catholic Church)

steps.text: Keep taking new burgher loans, upgrade centers of trade
Prospering Times event: option 2 (new center of trade)
steps.note: Trade power went from 0.9 to 14.5 for him

chain: Start St Peter's Basilica at 1,000 ducats
Get it to tier 1 before the commissioning event
steps.note: The event bumps it a tier

chain: Take admin tech 8 a bit early
steps.note: Fixes governing capacity

steps.text: Switch to level 2 advisors
Radical Reforms event: fire both advisors, take the points, rehire

1 to 3 nations left in Italy: merchants back to Maximize Profit and reposition
Admin tech 7: Trade ideas (Europe) or Religious (crusades)
Tier 4 reform: Head of the Catholic Church
Tier 5 reform
Annex diplo-vassals after 10 years. Lower autonomy

Full-state everything you get from subjects

Patrimony of St Peter mission (6 provinces in Marche and Emilia-Romagna)

steps.text: Venice again when the truce ends, with Austria

steps.text: Optional: hit Castile when France attacks them, for Valencia's cores
Florence: full annex is fine now

phases.name: Finish Italy
phases.intro: Milan is usually the biggest one left, since you allied them early.

have: St Peter's Basilica at tier 1 or 2

steps.text: Milan in about 3 wars, first for Genoa (5 provinces)
steps.note: Too much AE to take it all at once

steps.text: Keep the stronger of France and Austria, break with the other
steps.note: Use one to beat the other, then turn on the first

steps.text: Subjects divert trade when they're loyal
Become Defender of the Faith
Conquer Trent
steps.note: Needed for the Kingdom of God

steps.text: Declare the Kingdom of God

phases.name: 1507 benchmarks

Level 3 advisors
Courthouses, workshops, churches and marketplaces built
